title: The Operations Floor
intro: Big Sox Studios has a small crew of purpose-built AI agents handling infrastructure and smart-home work. They have defined jobs, limited permissions, and considerably more documentation than most fictional robots.
definition: These aren't generic chatbots with employee names pasted on them. Big Sox Studios agents are persistent, purpose-built workers with defined identities, jobs, tools, permissions, operational boundaries, and continuing responsibilities.
toolingNote: ChatGPT, Work, Codex, and other AI platforms help build and operate Big Sox Studios, but they are tools and collaborators—not employees.

otto.hook: Keeps the servers running, the services behaving, and the terminal commands away from Greg whenever possible.
otto.job: Otto is the infrastructure operator for the systems behind Big Sox Studios. He handles the boring-but-important work that keeps everything else available: services, deployments, diagnostics, server operations, and carefully bounded privileged actions.
otto.why: So routine infrastructure work doesn't require Greg to become the world's most reluctant part-time Linux administrator.
examples: Diagnose why a service stopped working.
Check the health of the server and supporting services.
Restart or deploy an approved service.
Verify that an infrastructure change actually worked.
Handle bounded maintenance jobs through the studio's agent runtime.
Produce evidence instead of simply declaring, “looks good to me.”
otto.boundaries: Otto is not supposed to freestyle with production infrastructure. His access is deliberately bounded, sensitive actions have controls around them, and a command completing successfully is not the same thing as the job being verified.
otto.current: Active and operational. Otto is the established infrastructure operator in the current agent lineup.
otto.personality: If the server is boring, healthy, and nobody has to think about it, Otto considers that an excellent day.

porter.hook: Turns “I wish the house did this” into Home Assistant automations—with backups, approvals, verification, and a healthy fear of breaking the lights.
porter.job: Porter is the builder for Home Assistant. He takes natural-language ideas and turns them into controlled smart-home changes, especially automations and scripts.
porter.why: Because “make the hallway lights do something smarter” should eventually be a request, not a Saturday afternoon YAML project.
examples: Inspect the existing Home Assistant configuration before making a change.
Back up affected configuration before mutation.
Apply an approved change, verify the result, and roll it back when necessary.
porter.boundaries: Porter has isolated Home Assistant access and does not inherit Otto's infrastructure privileges. Changes are designed around approval, backup, verification, and rollback rather than unrestricted control.
porter.current: Operational, but still onboarding into the full Builder role. Broader capabilities—especially richer dashboard work and more of the intended Builder feature set—are still being developed.
porter.personality: Porter measures twice, backs up three times, and would really prefer you not unplug the hub halfway through.

trace.hook: Future smart-home watchdog. She has a name, a job description, and absolutely no permission to touch anything yet.
trace.job: Trace is planned as the Home Guardian: the agent that watches the smart home rather than building it.
trace.why: A smart home isn't especially smart if something quietly breaks on Tuesday and nobody discovers it until Friday.
examples: Monitor Home Assistant and smart-home health.
Notice unusual failures or degraded behavior.
Connect symptoms across devices and systems.
Eventually support carefully bounded remediation where that is safe and appropriate.
trace.boundaries: Trace is not built yet. She does not currently monitor, diagnose, or remediate anything, and the future version is intended to stay within carefully defined permissions and operational boundaries.
trace.current: Pre-hire. Trace is planned, not operational, and her monitoring/remediation capabilities are future work.
trace.personality: Trace hasn't started work yet, which technically gives her the best incident record in the company.

relationship.title: How they work together
relationship.intro: Their jobs overlap enough to cooperate, but their responsibilities and permissions stay deliberately separate.
relationship.otto: Runs and verifies the infrastructure underneath the operation.
relationship.porter: Builds and changes things inside Home Assistant.
relationship.trace: Will watch, diagnose, and eventually help respond when the smart home misbehaves.
